questions.question: Why did Meg and Simone's big creation fall down?
questions.explanation: This question helps children remember how not working together made their creation weak, connecting the event to the idea that teamwork makes things stronger.

questions.question: How did Meg and Simone feel at the beginning when they worked alone?
questions.explanation: This question helps children notice the feelings of Meg and Simone when they didn’t get along, which shows that not working together can make people upset or frustrated.

questions.question: What happened when Meg and Simone decided to help each other?
questions.explanation: Children will see the positive change that happens when the characters start working together, highlighting the benefit of teamwork.

questions.question: Have you ever built something or played a game with a friend? What happened when you worked together?
questions.explanation: This question lets children think about their own lives and connect the story to their experiences, helping them see why working together is important.

questions.question: Why do you think Meg and Simone became friends at the end of the story?
questions.explanation: Children will consider how sharing and teamwork can help people become friends, tying it back to the moral lesson.

questions.question: If you and a friend each had different ideas for a game, what could you do to play together?
questions.explanation: This question encourages problem-solving and thinking about how to combine ideas, just like in the story.

questions.question: What can happen if we don't listen to each other's ideas when we work together?
questions.explanation: Responding to this helps children understand that listening is a big part of teamwork and friendships.

questions.question: Can you think of something amazing you could make or do by sharing ideas with your friends?
questions.explanation: This question encourages children to be creative and imagine what teamwork can look like in their own lives.

moral: When we work together and share ideas, we can create amazing things and make new friends.
learning_objectives: Children will understand the story's main events and the importance of teamwork.
Children will be able to describe how sharing ideas and working together can help everyone succeed.
Children will connect the story's lessons to their own life situations with friends and teamwork.
Children will practice reflecting on feelings and actions in group settings.
discussion_points: Why is it sometimes hard to work with others?
What are some ways we can listen to each other's ideas when we play or build together?
How does working with friends make things more fun or easier?
Can you share a time when you and a friend worked on something together? What happened?
What new things could we try making together in our class or at home?
